headline: New law puts named officials in charge of improving how federal agencies deliver benefits and services to the public.
what_it_does: The White House budget office (OMB) must name a senior official as the Federal Government Service Delivery Lead to coordinate efforts across the government to improve services. Each agency head is made responsible for improving how the agency delivers benefits and services. Each agency must also name a senior official to lead improvements to its services and to the ways people interact with it, such as mail, phone, and websites.

who_it_affects.group: Individuals, businesses, and organizations that get benefits or services from federal agencies
who_it_affects.how: Agencies must assign officials to work on improving how those benefits and services are delivered by mail, phone, website, and other channels.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agency heads and senior officials
who_it_affects.how: Agency heads become responsible for service delivery, and each agency must name a senior official to coordinate and carry out improvements.
OMB must name a senior official to coordinate service improvement efforts across the federal government.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 4, 2025; the summary does not give specific deadlines.
